les: Elke klank begin by iets wat vibreer
kaps_punt: Vibrasies en klank. Musiekinstrumente maak geluide deur vibrasies; die klank beweeg altyd uitwaarts vanaf die deel wat vibreer; ons kan vibrasies voel of hoor; die vibrasies beweeg deur materiale soos lug, water, plastiek, metaal en hout.

items.bewering: Sit jou hand plat teen jou keel en neurie 'n bekende wysie. Onder jou vingers voel jy hoe iets in jou keel vinnig bewe.
items.blok: Voel dit self teen jou keel
items.bron: Alberta Health, 'How your voice works' (myhealth.alberta.ca) and Weill Cornell voice centre (voice.weill.cornell.edu, 'Normal Voice Function'): humming is voiced, the vocal folds in the larynx vibrate, and the buzz can be felt with fingers on the front of the throat; folds vibrate 100+ times a second.

items.bewering: Hou nou op met neurie ... Die bewing hou saam met die klank op, en jou hand voel niks meer nie. Begin weer neurie en die bewing kom dadelik terug.
items.blok: Voel dit self teen jou keel
items.bron: Same voice sources (myhealth.alberta.ca; voice.weill.cornell.edu): the felt buzz is the vocal-fold vibration that produces voicing, so it is present only while voicing; the whisper-versus-voice hand test shows it vanishes without voicing.

items.bewering: Om te vibreer beteken om baie vinnig heen en weer te beweeg.
items.bron: Oxford Dictionaries entry 'vibrate' (mirrored at kamus.sabda.org): 'move continuously and rapidly to and fro'; dictionary.com: quiver, oscillate.

items.bewering: Die beweging gaan net oor 'n baie klein entjie.
items.bron: ASA Standards glossary, 'eardrum' (asastandards.org/terms/eardrum): eardrum displacement for a 1000 Hz tone at threshold is about 10 nm, and about 0.1 mm for low tones at the threshold of feeling. Sound-producing vibrations are small-amplitude.

items.bewering: Jy kan die vibrasie in jou keel en dié van 'n trom se vel voel.
items.bron: Voice sources above for the throat; HyperPhysics drum pages (hyperphysics.gsu.edu/hbase/Music/bdrum.html) and Penn State acoustics animations (acs.psu.edu/drussell/Demos/MembraneCircle) on the struck drumhead's whole-membrane vibration, which is large enough at the (0,1) mode to be felt by touch.

items.bewering: Mense wat nie kan hoor nie, kan vibrasies voel, en party van hulle beleef musiek so.
items.bron: University of Washington News, 27 Nov 2001, 'Brains of deaf people rewire to hear music' (Dean Shibata fMRI study: deaf subjects process vibration in the auditory cortex); Seattle Times archive 2002, 'Percussionist Glennie hears with her body' (profoundly deaf percussionist Evelyn Glennie feels music through her body). 'Party van hulle' is correctly narrowed.

items.bewering: Ander vibrasies is te klein om te voel, en dan hoor jy hulle net.
items.bron: ASA Standards glossary 'eardrum': audible displacement (~10 nm) is thousands of times smaller than the threshold of feeling (~0.1 mm), so many vibrations are heard and not felt. Read as 'some vibrations are too small to feel and are only heard', which is how the sentence is worded ('Ander', not 'Alle').

items.bewering: Elke musiekinstrument het 'n deel wat vibreer om sy klank te maak.
items.bron: Hornbostel-Sachs classification (Wikipedia, 'List of aerophones by Hornbostel-Sachs number'; EPFL graphsearch concept 142753): aerophones are instruments whose sound comes from a body of VIBRATING AIR, without strings or membranes and without the instrument itself vibrating appreciably. UNSW Music Acoustics, 'Flute acoustics' (newt.phys.unsw.edu.au/jw/fluteacoustics.html): in a flute the player's air jet and the air column inside the tube are what oscillate, not the tube. So 'every instrument' is right about vibration but wrong that the vibrating thing is always a PART of the instrument. A Grade 4 learner making a straw whistle or blowing across a bottle, and looking for the 'part' that vibrates, is led astray.
items.regstelling: Keep the universal claim about vibration and drop 'a part': every musical instrument makes its sound with something that vibrates. In a drum or a guitar it is a part of the instrument (the skin, the string); in a flute or a recorder it is the air inside it.

items.bewering: Slaan 'n trom en die vel bo-op begin vinnig op en af vibreer.
items.bron: HyperPhysics drum and snare-drum pages (hyperphysics.gsu.edu/hbase/Music/bdrum.html, snare.html); Penn State acoustics animations, circular membrane: the struck head vibrates in and out (perpendicular to its surface).

items.bewering: Pluk 'n kitaar se snaar en jy sien die snaar self vibreer.
items.bron: West Texas A&M, 'Science Questions with Surprising Answers' (wtamu.edu/~cbaird, 2014): a plucked guitar string visibly blurs because the eye cannot track its vibration.

items.bewering: In albei gevalle vibreer die deel eerste, en die klank kom daarvan af.
items.bron: Physics Classroom, 'Sound is a Mechanical Wave' (a wave is created by a vibrating object that introduces energy into the medium). Note for the person reading: UNSW Music Acoustics, guitar intro (newt.phys.unsw.edu.au/~jw/guitar/intro_engl.html) says the strings themselves radiate hardly any sound and the bridge and body radiate most of it. The sentence holds as 'the sound originates from the string's vibration', which is true; it is not a claim that the string itself radiates the sound, and no correction is needed.

items.bewering: Niks vibreer sommer vanself nie, en iemand of iets moet dit aan die beweeg kry.
items.bron: Physics Classroom, 'Sound is a Mechanical Wave' and its lesson notes (direct.physicsclassroom.com): a vibrating source must introduce energy into the medium; a vibration requires an initial input of energy (strike, pluck, blow, or driving by another vibration).

items.bewering: Waar jy ook al rondom 'n trom staan, hoor jy hom ... voor en agter die trom en aan albei kante. Die klank kies nie een rigting nie, en dit gaan na alle kante toe.
items.blok: Die klank gaan na alle kante toe
items.bron: Oak National Academy, 'Travelling vibrations' (thenational.academy) and ISVR Southampton acoustics tutorial (resource.isvr.soton.ac.uk): sound spreads outward in all directions from a vibrating source. Sources need not radiate EQUALLY in all directions, but the lesson only claims it is heard all round, which is true for a drum.

items.bewering: Dit beweeg altyd van die vibrerende vel af na buite toe.
items.blok: Die klank gaan na alle kante toe
items.bron: Oak National Academy 'Travelling vibrations'; Physics Classroom 'Sound is a Mechanical Wave' (tuning-fork example: disturbance passed outward from the source to adjacent air molecules).

items.bewering: Dit is nie wat gebeur nie, en niks vlieg van die trom af weg nie.
items.blok: Niks vlieg van die trom af na jou toe nie
items.bron: Physics Classroom, 'Sound - Detailed Help' (physicsclassroom.com/mop/m13) and 'Longitudinal Waves and Tuning Forks': a sound wave transports energy without transporting matter; there is no net displacement of the air.

items.bewering: Die vel stoot die lug wat teen hom staan 'n klein entjie weg. Daardie lug stoot die lug langsaan en gaan dan terug na sy plek. So loop die stoot van lug tot lug tot by jou oor. Die lug self bly waar dit is en waai nie na jou toe nie.
items.blok: Niks vlieg van die trom af na jou toe nie
items.bron: Physics Classroom, 'Longitudinal Waves and Tuning Forks' (air molecules vibrate about a fixed position; no net displacement); Oak National Academy 'Sound waves' (particles bump their neighbours and bounce back, oscillating about a fixed point). Mapping checked: a learner extending the chain-of-pushes picture reaches correct conclusions (the push passes on, the air stays, it needs air to pass through). It omits the rarefaction half of each cycle, an acceptable simplification that leads nowhere false.

items.bewering: Lug is die gewone pad, en die trom se klank kom so by jou uit.
items.bron: Physics Classroom lesson notes, 'Sound is a Mechanical Wave': typically the medium is air, though it could be any material such as water or steel.

items.bewering: Vibrasies loop ook deur materiale soos hout, metaal, plastiek en water.
items.bron: Engineering ToolBox, 'Solids and Metals - Speed of Sound' (engineeringtoolbox.com/sound-speed-solids-d_713.html): sound speeds listed for steel (~5900 m/s), hardwood (~3960 m/s) and plastics (acrylic 2680, nylon 2620, polyethylene 1950 m/s); DOSITS (dosits.org, University of Rhode Island) on water as an effective medium for sound.

items.bewering: Lê jou oor plat op 'n houttafel en tik lig met een vinger so ver as wat jou arm kan reik. Dieselfde ligte tik klink harder deur die hout as wanneer jou kop regop is.
items.bron: OCR 'Sound Transmission Experiments' (ocr.org/learn/activities) describes the ear-on-table demonstration; phys-l physics-teachers' list, Feb 2005 (phys-l.org/archives/2005/02_2005/msg00427.html), confirms the effect is real and explains it by more of the tap's energy going into the table and reaching an ear pressed to it. The lesson compares the same tap at the same distance, ear-on-wood versus head upright, and states no cause, so the observation as worded is true. It does not say sound grows louder as it travels through wood, which would be false.

items.bewering: Dieselfde gebeur wanneer iemand aan 'n metaalhek of 'n plastiekpyp tik.
items.bron: Engineering ToolBox sound-speed table (metals and plastics both conduct sound); same coupling explanation as the table (phys-l, 2005). Read in context as ear against the gate or pipe.

items.bewering: Klank loop ook deur water, soos wanneer jy met jou kop onder die water luister terwyl iemand teen die bad tik.
items.bron: HealthDay / Acoustical Society of America 2011, 'Underwater, Humans Hear Through Their Bones' (US Navy study; also reported by News24, 21 Jul 2012): people hear underwater, mainly by bone conduction; DOSITS on water as a sound medium.

items.bewering: Klank het altyd iets nodig om deur te beweeg. Daar moet 'n materiaal soos lug, water, plastiek, metaal of hout in die pad wees. Sonder so 'n materiaal kan die klank nie by jou uitkom nie.
items.bron: Physics Classroom, 'Sound is a Mechanical Wave' (bell-in-a-jar: once the air is removed the ringing bell can no longer be heard); NASA eClips SpotLite teacher guide 'Sound waves and medium' (assets.science.nasa.gov): sound does not travel in a vacuum such as deep space.

items.bewering: Jou buiteoor is die deel wat jy aan die kant van jou kop sien.
items.blok: Hoe die klank by jou oor inkom
items.bron: RNID, 'How the ear works' (rnid.org.uk): 'The outer ear is made up of the pinna, which is the part you can see on the side of your head, and the ear canal.' Afrikaans Wikipedia, 'Oor': 'Die buitenste oor sluit die sigbare deel van die oor in, die uitwendige oorkanaal en die oortrom.' Dutch hospital leaflets (bravis.nl, webwoordenboek.nl): buitenoor = oorschelp + uitwendige gehoorgang. The visible part is only part of the outer ear; the ear canal belongs to the outer ear too.
items.regstelling: Make the outer ear include the ear canal: the outer ear is the part you see on the side of your head together with the ear canal (gehoorgang) that leads inward from it. If a separate name is wanted for the visible part alone, the writer should use an established Afrikaans term for the pinna and verify it; 'oorskulp' could not be confirmed in any source found.

items.bewering: Dit vang die klank en lei dit in 'n klein gangetjie in, die gehoorgang.
items.blok: Hoe die klank by jou oor inkom
items.bron: RNID 'How the ear works'; ASHA 'How We Hear' (asha.org): the pinna gathers sound and channels it into the ear canal. (Correct as a statement about the visible part; the naming fault is in the previous item.)

items.bewering: Aan die einde van die gehoorgang sit 'n dun velletjie wat styf gespan is. Ons noem dit die trommelvlies, en die klank laat daardie velletjie vibreer.
items.blok: Hoe die klank by jou oor inkom
items.bron: Afrikaans Wikipedia 'Oor': 'Die trommelvlies of oortrom is oor die binneste end van die buitenste gehoorgang gespan', so thin it is almost transparent; RNID: sound travelling down the canal sets the eardrum moving.

items.bewering: By die trom kom die klank van die vibrasie af, en hier is dit andersom.
items.blok: Hoe die klank by jou oor inkom
items.bron: Mapping checked against HyperPhysics drum pages (struck membrane vibrates and radiates sound) and RNID (incoming sound sets the eardrum vibrating). The reversal maps correctly: drum skin = vibration makes sound; eardrum = sound makes vibration. Both are thin stretched membranes, which the lesson's own wording supports, and a learner extending the comparison is not led to anything false.

items.bewering: Agter die velletjie gee die klein gehoorbeentjies die vibrasie aan tot by die binneoor.
items.blok: Hoe die klank by jou oor inkom
items.bron: RNID 'How the ear works': the malleus, incus and stapes carry the vibrations from the eardrum to the inner ear; Afrikaans Wikipedia 'Oor': gehoorbeentjies = hamer, aambeeld, stiebeuel.

items.bewering: Die binneoor stuur 'n boodskap na jou brein, en dan hoor jy die trom.
items.blok: Hoe die klank by jou oor inkom
items.bron: RNID 'How the ear works' and ASHA 'How We Hear': hair cells in the cochlea turn the vibration into electrical signals that the auditory nerve carries to the brain, which recognises them as sounds.

items.bewering: vibreer: Om baie vinnig heen en weer te beweeg.
items.bron: Oxford 'vibrate' (via kamus.sabda.org): move continuously and rapidly to and fro. True read on its own.

items.bewering: buiteoor: Die deel van jou oor wat jy aan jou kop kan sien.
items.bron: RNID 'How the ear works' (outer ear = pinna plus ear canal); Afrikaans Wikipedia 'Oor' (buitenste oor includes the visible part and the outer ear canal). Read on its own, the entry defines the outer ear as the visible part only, which is false.
items.regstelling: Define the outer ear as the part of your ear you can see on your head together with the ear canal that leads inward from it, consistent with the corrected study sentence.

items.bewering: gehoorgang: Die klein gangetjie wat van jou buiteoor na die trommelvlies loop.
items.bron: RNID 'How the ear works'; Afrikaans Wikipedia 'Oor' ('buitenste gehoorgang', part of the outer ear). Read on its own, 'from your outer ear to the eardrum' places the ear canal outside the outer ear; the canal is part of the outer ear and runs from the visible part to the eardrum.
items.regstelling: Say the ear canal runs from the part of the ear you can see to the eardrum, or that it is the small passage inside the outer ear leading to the eardrum, so that it does not put the canal outside the outer ear.

items.bewering: trommelvlies: 'n Dun velletjie in jou oor wat vibreer wanneer klank dit tref.
items.bron: Afrikaans Wikipedia 'Oor' (thin, stretched across the inner end of the ear canal); RNID (sound sets the eardrum moving). True read on its own.

items.bewering: gehoorbeentjies: Drie klein beentjies agter die trommelvlies wat die vibrasie verder aangee.
items.bron: RNID 'How the ear works' (three ossicles in the middle ear carry vibrations from the eardrum to the inner ear); Afrikaans Wikipedia 'Oor' (hamer, aambeeld, stiebeuel). True read on its own.

items.bewering: binneoor: Die deel diep in jou oor wat boodskappe na jou brein stuur.
items.bron: RNID and ASHA (cochlear hair cells produce signals carried by the auditory nerve to the brain); Afrikaans Wikipedia 'Oor' (binneoor = koglea plus labirint, deepest part). True read on its own.

opsomming: Two faults to fix: the lesson calls only the visible part of the ear the outer ear, but the outer ear includes the ear canal too (the study sentence and both the 'buiteoor' and 'gehoorgang' entries); and 'every instrument has a part that vibrates' is not true of a flute or recorder, where the air inside vibrates. Everything else was checked against sources and is correct, including the air-to-air push picture and the drum-and-eardrum reversal.
